research_question: How can a robot select time-varying normal–tangential impedance online during continuous soft-contact scanning to minimize a joint force-regulation, trajectory-tracking, and contact-loss or slip objective while respecting wrench and interaction-energy constraints across material, geometry, sliding-condition, and contact-history shifts absent from its calibration data?
observed_phenomenon: The accepted evidence separates three capabilities that have not yet been closed into one continuous-soft-contact optimal-impedance problem. A Hunt–Crossley-based single-critic controller selects impedance optimally only after task-specific environment identification and without explicit force, energy, delay, or solver-failure constraints; robotic-ultrasound and deformable-contact MPC model finite-area sliding contact but keep impedance predefined; model-agnostic six-dimensional admittance regulates wrench accurately in bounded regimes but does not solve online optimal impedance selection and warns that time-varying impedance can lose passivity. Continuous scanning meanwhile changes material response, geometry, tangential resistance, and history, so the gain choice that best trades force regulation, motion quality, and contact safety need not remain fixed or transferable beyond calibration.
scope_and_conditions: Continuous sliding or scanning of a rigid ultrasound-like probe over compliant finite-area surfaces, with measurable robot pose or indentation, normal and tangential wrench, commanded and rendered impedance, scanning velocity, and an independent task-quality signal. The decision variables are bounded normal and tangential stiffness and damping updated more slowly than the inner motion loop. Evaluation must include held-out changes in stiffness or relaxation, local curvature or thickness, direction or speed, dwell or loading history, tangential resistance, and external disturbance; must compare under matched data, sensing, compute, objective, inner-loop bandwidth, and safety budgets; and must measure force/wrench regulation, trajectory or speed tracking, contact loss or slip, impedance variation, real-time feasibility, and an independent scanning endpoint. The problem excludes universal soft-body modeling, unrestricted online exploration, patient-specific clinical efficacy, universal tissue-injury limits, and the presumption that any particular contact model, learning architecture, MPC formulation, critic, or passivity device is the solution.
why_it_matters: Impedance is the robot's direct mechanical policy for trading tracking precision against compliant and safe interaction. If it cannot be selected reliably as contact conditions change, stronger contact models, estimators, or learning modules do not by themselves produce better control. Solving this problem would connect optimal impedance planning, continuous finite-area soft-contact control, and enforceable interaction constraints in a form that can be tested against strong model-aware and model-agnostic baselines rather than merely improving contact-model fit.
value_if_yes: A positive result would establish an online impedance-selection principle that measurably improves the joint force–motion–contact outcome over fixed, scheduled, model-agnostic, and contact-aware predefined-impedance baselines on held-out contact shifts, while satisfying predeclared wrench, energy, and real-time limits. It would also identify the smallest set of state, uncertainty, and constraint information needed for that control improvement without requiring unsafe excitation or per-condition retuning.
value_if_no: A negative result would show that robust fixed or conventionally scheduled impedance, model-agnostic wrench feedback, or predefined-impedance contact-aware MPC is already decision-equivalent within practical margins across the declared envelope, or that partial observability and safe-excitation limits make further online optimality unattainable. That result would prevent unnecessary learning, identification, sensing, and optimization complexity and would move effort toward better inner-loop rendering, conservative constraints, or narrower operating envelopes.

plausible_explanations.explanation: The optimal impedance changes under held-out contact shifts because stiffness and damping alter force transients, tangential motion, and contact stability through a contact-dependent closed-loop map that is not invariant to material, geometry, friction, or history.

A strong measured-wrench feedback or contact-aware predictive controller absorbs most contact variation, leaving little incremental value for online optimal impedance selection once objectives, constraints, and tuning budgets are matched.
The apparent benefit of adaptive impedance is caused mainly by unequal tuning, estimator leakage, richer sensing, or a weaker baseline rather than by a transferable gain-selection principle.

Partial observability prevents the controller from distinguishing contact states before different gain choices are needed, so safe near-optimal selection requires either a compact predictive state, calibrated uncertainty, or a deliberately restricted claim envelope.

Hard wrench, energy, computation, and inner-loop rendering constraints dominate the admissible gain set, so the main unsolved difficulty is safe feasible decision making rather than nominal cost minimization.

measurement_validity: Use synchronized, independently calibrated six-axis wrench, robot pose or indentation, commanded and rendered stiffness and damping, scanning speed, solver timing, constraint activity, and an independent task-quality measure. Separate identification and controller-development conditions from held-out specimens, regions, curvatures, relaxation times, speeds, directions, dwell histories, and disturbances. Predeclare the joint objective, safety constraints, equivalence or improvement margins, failure handling, and computation budget; randomize repeated conditions; verify sensor bandwidth, delay, drift, saturation, gain-rendering fidelity, and contact-state observability; and report transient, steady-state, failure-inclusive, and uncertainty-aware results.
artifact_or_confound_alternatives: Unequal hyperparameter, gain, model, data, sensing, horizon, or compute budgets across controllers
Test-condition or specimen leakage into contact identification, policy training, model selection, or normalization
Inner-loop tracking and impedance-rendering error misattributed to the high-level impedance selector
Force/torque drift, filtering, delay, saturation, gravity compensation, or cross-axis coupling
Surface-normal, indentation, contact-area, or local-geometry reconstruction error
Changes in coupling medium, lubrication, temperature, hydration, adhesion, friction, or specimen aging
Optimizer infeasibility, timeout, warm-start bias, actuator saturation, fallback logic, or emergency-stop behavior
Task-quality changes caused by perception or image-processing shift rather than contact control
independent_support: j4KJ1EdUyYAJ directly establishes identified-model single-critic optimal impedance and exposes limits in time variation, safe exploration, constraints, and physical certification.
USER-TRO-2022-3216078 independently establishes online constrained Cartesian stiffness-and-damping planning without a soft-contact model, preventing novelty from online gain optimization alone.
QPuQ4sfxSTIJ establishes continuous robotic-ultrasound soft-contact MPC with finite-area sliding effects but no adaptive optimal impedance.
ZDySGaNsMn8J independently establishes real-time deformable-contact-aware constrained MPC while keeping impedance predefined.
USER-TASE-2023-3282974 establishes strong model-agnostic six-dimensional compliant control and documents the passivity or oscillation risk of ideal time-varying impedance.
_8NXx8-VkcgJ, USER-TUFFC-2011-1961, and Ubx3Xkv4y2kJ support contact dynamics and wrench-capacity changes with relaxation and history while constraining online identifiability claims.
9vRJMR2dgG4J establishes a strong uncertainty-tightened predictive-control comparator but limits its guarantees to static-output uncertainty.
phenomenon_prevalence_or_effect_scale: The conflict recurs across optimal impedance interaction, robotic-ultrasound scanning, deformable-contact MPC, six-dimensional compliant control, soft-tissue force control, and uncertainty-aware force MPC. Accepted studies report meaningful nominal improvements from optimal impedance, contact-aware prediction, or uncertainty handling, yet those gains are each bounded by prior identification, predefined impedance, restricted geometry or material, static uncertainty, or qualitative human evaluation. The prevalence is therefore established across adjacent control families, while the size and robustness of the benefit from online optimal impedance under held-out continuous soft-contact shifts remain unmeasured.
decision_owner_and_threshold: The scientific decision owner is the independent Problem Quality and Problem Novelty sequence followed by the human problem Gate. Later empirical support requires that, under matched resources, an online impedance selector reduce a predeclared joint force–motion–contact-risk cost or its regret relative to a condition-informed offline reference by more than a sensor- and task-relevant margin on held-out conditions; satisfy all predeclared wrench, contact-loss or slip, interaction-energy, actuator, and computation limits; and outperform the strongest fixed, scheduled, model-agnostic, contact-aware predefined-impedance, and uncertainty-aware comparators without material loss on any primary endpoint. Failure handling and infeasible or timed-out decisions count against the method.
falsifier: Across the declared held-out material, geometry, speed, direction, history, tangential-load, and disturbance conditions, the strongest matched conventional baselines remain equivalent to or better than online impedance selection on the joint objective and every primary safety and task endpoint; or any apparent improvement disappears after equalizing data, sensing, computation, tuning, inner-loop rendering, and fallback behavior; or no selector can improve the objective without violating wrench, energy, contact, actuator, or real-time limits. Any of these outcomes falsifies the claim that a new general online optimal-impedance principle is needed for the stated envelope.
feasible_discriminating_probe: Construct a repeated-measures benchtop continuous-scanning benchmark with multiple soft phantoms spanning stiffness and relaxation, at least two local curvatures or thicknesses, controlled speed and direction changes, dwell and loading histories, tangential resistance changes, and bounded disturbances, with entire specimens or regions held out. Establish a condition-informed offline impedance reference and compare robust fixed impedance, conventional gain scheduling, model-agnostic six-dimensional admittance, online constrained impedance planning, a reproduced identified-contact optimal-impedance baseline, and contact-aware predefined-impedance MPC under one objective and matched resources. Measure joint cost and reference regret, transient wrench, trajectory and speed error, contact loss or slip, constraint violations, energy injection, solve time, fallback frequency, and an independent scanning-quality endpoint; use ablations only after an overall control benefit is demonstrated.
closest_prior_answer: The closest integrated priors cover complementary but incomplete slices: j4KJ1EdUyYAJ learns optimal impedance from an identified scalar Hunt–Crossley environment without explicit interaction constraints or abrupt shift handling; USER-TRO-2022-3216078 plans stiffness and damping online under tracking constraints without soft-contact mechanics; QPuQ4sfxSTIJ and ZDySGaNsMn8J embed finite-area or distributed-pressure contact in real-time MPC but leave impedance predefined; USER-TASE-2023-3282974 achieves accurate six-dimensional compliant control without an optimal gain-selection objective and shows risks in time-varying impedance; 9vRJMR2dgG4J tightens force constraints under static-output uncertainty. No bound prior selects normal–tangential impedance online for continuous soft-contact scanning while jointly evaluating held-out optimality, force–motion performance, contact failure, interaction-energy constraints, and real-time feasibility under matched strong baselines.
uncertainties: Whether a useful condition-informed offline optimum can be defined without privileging one controller class
Which force–motion–contact-risk objective and equivalence margins reflect practical scanning value
Whether normal and tangential impedance should be coupled or can be optimized separately
Which contact variations are observable before a gain change is required
Whether safe task excitation is sufficient for online adaptation or uncertainty calibration
How interaction-energy constraints should be defined for nonzero force and motion references
Whether real-time optimization remains feasible with failure-inclusive safety checks
How phantom results transfer to ex-vivo or in-vivo conditions without making a clinical claim
